renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: identity_vs_coverage
  title: Identity against coverage of the target
  description: |-
    Each point is a query genome aligned to the target: the share of the target its one-to-one alignment covers on the horizontal axis and the percent identity on the vertical axis. Size is the aligned length and colour the number of sequences in the query. It answers whether a genome is distant or only fragmented.
    How to read: identity falls with divergence, so a distant genome sits low. Coverage also falls with divergence and with assembly gaps, so a point to the left of genomes of similar identity lost coverage to a fragmented assembly, which the colour confirms. Open the distance and parameter tiles for the same pairs.
    Note: there is no standard way to compute nucleotide identity, so the value here is the one nf-core/pairgenomealign reports (gaps counted as mismatches).
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median alignment identity of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of LAST.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/pairgenomealign/master/docs/output.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
    color_col: query_sequences
    x_title: Target covered by the one-to-one alignment (%)
    y_title: Alignment identity (%)
  roles:
    x: target_aligned_pct
    y: percent_identity
    label: query
    size: aligned_bp

- component: figure
  title: Share of the target covered
  description: |-
    Each bar is a query genome with the share of the target genome its one-to-one alignment covers, coloured by percent identity. It answers which genomes align to most of the target.
    How to read: a short bar with a high identity colour is a close genome with a fragmented assembly or a real loss of sequence. A short bar with a low identity colour is simply a distant genome.
    Note: the one-to-one alignment keeps one copy of locally duplicated regions, so they count as missing in the other genome.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median share of the target covered of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of LAST.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/pairgenomealign/master/docs/output.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: query
    y: target_aligned_pct
    color: percent_identity
    labels:
      query: Query genome
      target_aligned_pct: Target covered (%)
      percent_identity: Identity (%)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: target_aligned_pct

- component: card
  id: identity_median
  title: Alignment identity
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median nucleotide percent identity of the one-to-one alignments and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how close the aligned genomes are to the target.
    How to read: closely related genomes sit near 100 percent, and the identity falls as genomes diverge. A wide box means the run mixes close and distant genomes.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/pairgenomealign/master/docs/output.md
  column: percent_identity
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: identity, with its spread
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: target_coverage
  title: Target covered
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of the target genome covered by the one-to-one alignment, and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how much of the target the queries reach.
    How to read: coverage below 100 percent is expected, since a one-to-one alignment leaves out duplicated and unalignable regions. A low tail marks genomes that are divergent or fragmented.
  column: target_aligned_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: coverage across genomes
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: genome_size
  title: Query genome length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median total length of the query genomes, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers whether the queries are of a similar size to the target.
    How to read: a query much longer or shorter than the rest has a different assembly completeness or a real size difference, which also lowers coverage.
  column: query_length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: genome length, with its spread

- component: card
  id: aligned_length
  title: Aligned length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median number of aligned base pairs in the one-to-one alignments, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how much sequence each alignment holds.
    How to read: compare it with the genome length card. A short aligned length for a genome of normal size means a divergent or fragmented query.
  column: aligned_bp
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: aligned length, with its spread

- component: card
  id: aligned_total
  title: Aligned bases in total
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total aligned base pairs over all pairs, and the strip shows the share held by the three genomes with the longest alignments. It answers whether the alignment is spread evenly over the queries.
    How to read: a share close to the number of genomes shown over the total means the queries align alike. A higher share points to a few genomes dominating.
  column: aligned_bp
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: concentration
  breakdown_col: query
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: share held by the top genomes

- component: interactive
  title: Identity range
  description: |-
    Select a range of percent identity to keep only the genome pairs inside it. It answers which pairs fall in a given divergence band.
    How to read: narrow the range to a band of closely related genomes, and every other tile follows.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: percent_identity

- component: table
  title: Alignment summary table
  description: |-
    Each row is a genome pair with the aligned length, identity with and without gaps, sequence counts and lengths of both genomes, and the share of each genome covered. It answers the exact numbers behind every tile and lets a row selection filter the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by identity to rank the pairs by divergence.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: query

- component: advanced_viz
  id: substitution_spectrum
  title: Substitution spectrum by query
  description: |-
    Each cell is the share of one directed substitution (a target base aligned to a different query base) among all substitutions in the one-to-one alignment of a query genome. It answers whether the substitution process looks alike across the queries.
    How to read: transitions (A to G, G to A, C to T, T to C) usually hold the largest shares, and genomes of similar divergence cluster together. A query whose row differs from the rest points to a different mutation process or a lower quality assembly.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/pairgenomealign/master/docs/output.md
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: query
    value_columns:
    - A_to_C_pct
    - A_to_G_pct
    - A_to_T_pct
    - C_to_A_pct
    - C_to_G_pct
    - C_to_T_pct
    - G_to_A_pct
    - G_to_C_pct
    - G_to_T_pct
    - T_to_A_pct
    - T_to_C_pct
    - T_to_G_pct

- component: advanced_viz
  id: saturation_scatter
  title: Transition to transversion ratio against distance
  description: |-
    Each point is a query genome: its p-distance to the target on the horizontal axis and its ratio of transitions to transversions on the vertical axis. Size is the number of alignment blocks and colour the number of gap columns on the query side. It answers whether the distant genomes are saturated.
    How to read: the ratio falls as multiple substitutions at one site hide the transitions, so distant genomes sit low and to the right. A point off that trend is a pair whose alignment or assembly deserves a look.
    Lines and annotations: no reference line is drawn, because the expected ratio depends on the species pair and the tool publishes no cut-off.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    color_col: query_gap_columns
    x_title: Substitutions per aligned column (p-distance)
    y_title: Transitions to transversions ratio
  roles:
    x: p_distance
    y: ts_tv_ratio
    label: query
    size: blocks

- component: figure
  title: K80 distance to the target
  description: |-
    Each bar is a query genome with its K80 distance to the target, the p-distance corrected for multiple substitutions with separate rates for transitions and transversions. It answers how diverged each query is.
    How to read: closely related genomes have short bars and distant genomes long ones. The correction matters for distant genomes only, so compare it with the raw p-distance in the table.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median K80 distance of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of LAST.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: query
    y: k80_distance
    color: k80_distance
    labels:
      query: Query genome
      k80_distance: K80 distance
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: k80_distance

- component: card
  id: k80_median
  title: K80 distance
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median K80 distance of the queries to the target and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how diverged the queries are on the whole.
    How to read: a wide box means the run mixes close and distant genomes, and a single distant genome pulls the upper whisker out.
  column: k80_distance
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: distance, with its spread
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: ts_tv_median
  title: Transition to transversion ratio
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median ratio of transitions to transversions over the alignments, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers whether the substitution process is similar across queries.
    How to read: a tight box means the queries mutate alike. A ratio that falls with distance is the sign of saturation.
  column: ts_tv_ratio
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: ratio, with its spread

- component: card
  id: blocks_median
  title: Alignment blocks
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median number of alignment blocks per genome pair, and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how fragmented the alignments are.
    How to read: more blocks come with more divergence and more rearrangements, so a pair far above the rest is either distant or fragmented.
  column: blocks
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: blocks across genomes

- component: card
  id: query_gap_median
  title: Gap columns on the query
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of alignment columns where the target has a base and the query a gap, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how much sequence the target holds that the query lacks.
    How to read: more gap columns come with divergence and with a more fragmented query assembly. Compare it with the target-side gaps in the table.
  column: query_gap_columns
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: gap columns, with their spread

- component: interactive
  title: Distance range
  description: |-
    Select a range of p-distance to keep only the genome pairs inside it. It answers which pairs fall in a given divergence band.
    How to read: narrow the range to a band of related genomes, and every other tile follows.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: p_distance

- component: table
  title: Distances and substitutions table
  description: |-
    Each row is a genome pair with its alignment blocks, counts of identical and substituted columns, transitions and transversions, gap columns, distances under four models and the substitution spectrum. It answers the exact numbers behind every tile and lets a row selection filter the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by distance to rank the queries by divergence.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: query

- component: advanced_viz
  id: synteny_ring
  title: Synteny between target and query
  description: |-
    Each chord is one of the longest one-to-one alignments, linking its locus on a target chromosome to its locus on a query chromosome, coloured by orientation and weighted by its matching bases. It answers which chromosomes of the two genomes share long collinear blocks.
    How to read: bundles of chords between the same two chromosomes are conserved synteny. Chords that fan out from one chromosome point to rearrangements, and inverted chords mark blocks that are reversed in the query.
    Note: only the longest alignments of each pair are kept, so short blocks do not appear.
  kind: genome_chord
  config:
    colour_by: category
  roles:
    chrom_a: chrom_a
    pos_a: pos_a
    chrom_b: chrom_b
    pos_b: pos_b
    label: label
    weight: weight
    category: category
    sample: query

- component: card
  id: links_total
  title: Synteny links
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of retained alignment links and the bar splits them by orientation, same strand or inverted. It answers how many long blocks are conserved and how many are reversed.
    How to read: most long blocks of closely related genomes keep their orientation. A large inverted share points to rearranged or distant genomes.
  column: label
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: category
  caption: links, by orientation
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: links_weight
  title: Matching bases in the links
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total matching bases of the retained links and the strip shows the share held by the three target chromosomes with the most. It answers whether the conserved blocks are spread over the genome.
    How to read: a high share means a few chromosomes hold most of the long blocks, which is expected for the largest chromosomes.
  column: weight
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: concentration
  breakdown_col: chrom_a
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: share held by the top chromosomes
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: links_identity
  title: Identity of the links
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percent identity of the retained links and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how conserved the long blocks are.
    How to read: identity of long blocks tracks the divergence of the pair. A wide box means the run mixes close and distant genomes.
  column: identity_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: identity, with its spread

- component: card
  id: links_span
  title: Length of the links
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median aligned length of the retained links and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how long the conserved blocks are.
    How to read: long blocks mean a well assembled and little rearranged pair. Short blocks mean the genomes are fragmented or rearranged.
  column: aligned_bp
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: link length, with its spread

- component: interactive
  title: Orientation
  description: |-
    Select same strand or inverted links to keep only those. It answers where the reversed blocks sit.
    How to read: pick inverted to see the rearranged regions in the ring and the table.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: category

- component: table
  title: Synteny links table
  description: |-
    Each row is a retained alignment link with its locus on both genomes, aligned length, identity, orientation and rank. It answers the exact coordinates behind each chord and lets a row selection filter the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by weight to list the longest blocks, and filter by orientation to list the inverted ones.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: label

- component: advanced_viz
  id: gap_cost_vs_identity
  title: Gap cost against training identity
  description: |-
    Each point is a query genome: the identity last-train measured on its training sample on the horizontal axis and the fitted cost of opening a deletion on the vertical axis, coloured by the score scale. It answers whether the fitted parameters follow the divergence of each pair.
    How to read: the costs track divergence, so pairs of similar identity sit at similar costs. A pair whose cost stands apart from genomes of similar identity is worth checking, since the parameters drive every alignment.
    Source: https://gitlab.com/mcfrith/last/-/raw/main/doc/last-train.rst
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    color_col: score_scale
    x_title: Identity of the training sample (%)
    y_title: Cost of opening a deletion
  roles:
    x: training_percent_identity
    y: deletion_open_cost
    label: query

- component: card
  id: training_identity
  title: Training identity
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median substitution identity of the training samples and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how similar the queries are to the target in the sample last-train used.
    How to read: the training sample is a pseudo-random subset of the query, so it tracks the whole-genome identity. A wide box means the run mixes close and distant genomes.
    Source: https://gitlab.com/mcfrith/last/-/raw/main/doc/last-train.rst
  column: training_percent_identity
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: identity, with its spread

- component: card
  id: gap_open_cost
  title: Deletion opening cost
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median cost of opening a deletion fitted by last-train, and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how expensive gaps are for a typical pair.
    How to read: last-train derives the costs from the rates of deletions and insertions it sees, so a closer genome gets a higher cost. A pair far from the others has unusual gap rates in its training sample.
    Source: https://gitlab.com/mcfrith/last/-/raw/main/doc/last-train.rst
  column: deletion_open_cost
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: costs across genomes
  headline: true

- component: table
  title: Fitted parameters table
  description: |-
    Each row is a genome pair with the training identity, score scale, gap opening and extension costs for deletions and insertions, and the strand setting. It answers the exact parameters used to align each pair.
    How to read: compare the costs of pairs with similar identity to spot an outlier.
